intro: Buying clothes and shoes: sizes, how they fit, and taking them or changing them.
p.probarse.consejo: It changes o to ue: «me pruebo». «Probar» is also tasting a little of something.
p.talla.consejo: It is used for clothes: «¿qué talla usa?». The word for shoes varies by country.
p.número.consejo: In this lesson, for shoes you say «número»: «el treinta y ocho». It is also «number».
p.probador.consejo: It comes from «probar»: the place to try things on. It ends in -dor, like «trabajador».
p.estrechas.consejo: It is feminine plural because it talks about «las botas». Its opposite is «anchas».
p.ancho.consejo: It is the opposite of «estrecho». It agrees: ancho, ancha, anchos, anchas.
p.cambiar.consejo: You change a size, a gift or money. It is regular: «cambio», «cambias».
p.tique.consejo: It is written «tique» in Spanish. Keep it if you want to exchange or return something.
p.botas.consejo: They are bought in pairs: «las botas». In the singular, «la bota».
p.ponerse.consejo: It takes an article: «me pongo el abrigo». The «me» changes with the person: «te pones».
p.quitarse.consejo: It takes an article: «me quito los zapatos». It is the opposite of «ponerse».
p.me las llevo.consejo: The middle word changes: «me lo llevo», «me la llevo», «me los llevo», «me las llevo».
p.me queda grande.consejo: It works like «gustar»: «me queda grande», but «me quedan grandes» if there are several.
p.devolver.consejo: It changes o to ue: «devuelvo», «devuelves». It is the same change as in «poder».
b1.texto:
To try something on: **¿Puedo probarme** esta camisa**?** With a pronoun: **¿Puedo probármela?** or **¿Me la puedo probar?**

The shop assistant asks **¿Qué talla usa?** for clothes and **¿Qué número usa?** for shoes; the words change by country.

To say how it fits you use **quedar**, like **gustar**: **me queda** bien, grande, pequeño, estrecho, ancho. The adjective agrees: **me quedan estrechas** (the boots).

To ask for another: **¿Tiene una talla más?** **¿Lo tiene en azul?**

To decide: **me lo llevo**, **me la llevo**, **me los llevo**, **me las llevo**.

To return or exchange something, keep **el tique**: the rules depend on each shop.
b2.f0.texto: Can I try these boots on?
b2.f1.texto: What shoe size do you wear?
b2.f3.texto: How do the boots fit you?
b2.f4.texto: They are a bit tight on me.
b2.f5.texto: Do you have a size bigger?
b2.f7.texto: You can exchange them with the receipt.
b4.texto:
With **probarse** and **poder** the pronoun has two places:

- **¿Puedo probármela?** (attached to the infinitive).
- **¿Me la puedo probar?** (before the conjugated verb).

**Quedar** agrees with the garment: **me queda estrecha** (the boot), **me quedan estrechas** (the boots).

To take your purchase, the pronoun agrees with the thing: **me lo / me la / me los / me las llevo**.

**Ponerse** and **quitarse** take an article with clothes: **me pongo el abrigo**, **me quito los zapatos**.
b4.e1.texto: The boots are tight on me.
b4.e2.texto: I put on the blue coat.
b5.f0.texto: The shoe shop smells of new leather and cardboard.
b5.f1.texto: The black boots wait in a row on a wooden shelf.
b5.f2.texto: A kind assistant brings a big box with the two boots.
b5.f3.texto: Lucía sits on a small bench.
b5.f4.texto: A long mirror gathers the afternoon light in its golden frame.
b5.f5.texto: Lucía puts on the first boot very carefully.
b5.f6.texto: The cold leather squeezes her toes a little.
b5.f7.texto: She walks slowly to the mirror and looks at her feet.
b5.f8.texto: The bigger boot hugs the foot like a glove.
b5.f9.texto: Lucía leaves the shop with the new boots in a bag.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done! «Las botas» is plural and so is the verb.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Queda» is singular. The boots are two.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Quedo» is «I stay». Here it is the boots that fit.
b7.o0.refuerzo: The talla is for clothes: shirts, dresses, coats.
b7.o1.refuerzo: The tique is the shopping receipt, not a measure.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That's it! Shoes have a número: el treinta y ocho.
b7.pregunta: In this lesson, what is the shoe measure called?
b8.traduccion: Do you have a bigger size
b9.o2.refuerzo: «La» is singular. The boots are several.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Me quito el abrigo» is taking it off your body.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Ponerse» is the opposite: putting clothes on.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Probarse» is putting something on to see if it fits.
b10.pregunta: Which verb means taking your coat off?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «Can I try it on?» (the dress).
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Me quito el abrigo» is what you do when it is hot.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Me pruebo» is to see if it fits, not because of the cold.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Well done! When it is cold you put your coat on.
b12.pregunta: It is cold. Which verb completes the sentence?
p.probarme.consejo: The «v» in «probar» sounds like «b». The pronoun «me» attaches to the verb.
p.usa.consejo: The «u» is short, and the stress is on «U». It means you wear that shoe size.
p.cambiarlas.consejo: «las» refers to the shoes. The verb is «cambiar» with «las» attached.
p.recoge.consejo: From «recoger». The «g» before «e» is «h», and the stress is on «KO».
p.bota.consejo: Shoes that cover the ankle. The «v» in other words sounds like «b», but here it is just «b».
p.guante.consejo: The «gu» before «a» is a hard «g», so it is «gu-AN-te».
